title: My experience with MTC Education’s XS momentum AI trading system — proceed with caution
author: Additional_Job8418
selftext:
I’m sharing this solely based on my own experience with Michael Sloggett and MTC Education’s XS momentum AI trading system. I’m not speaking for anyone else, and I’m not saying it is necessarily a complete scam. It may become profitable in the future, but I wish I had understood the costs, risks and inconsistencies before committing my own money.

My biggest concern was how widely the results varied between people supposedly using the same system. On the same trading day, one person could report a profit, another a significant loss, while Michael’s reported result could be materially different again.

The usual explanation was that accounts rebalanced at different times. However, I did not feel there was enough transparency about why the discrepancies could be so large or enough responsibility taken for delivering a reasonably consistent product. 

The drawdowns were acknowledged, but in my opinion they were greatly downplayed compared with the attention given to profitable days. Positive results were heavily promoted, while losing periods were often treated as temporary setbacks that would eventually recover.

In my own experience, I was up around 10% after the first month. During the second month, a decline of roughly 14% wiped out all of those gains and left me approximately -5% to where I started. This showed me how quickly a strong-looking return could disappear after only a few significant losses. 

When people questioned the discrepancies or raised concerns, I felt they were often given the same explanation about rebalancing times or told they could leave if they were unhappy, rather than the underlying problems being properly addressed.

The membership costs \*\*USD $200 per month\*\*. Someone starting with USD $500 would need to make \*\*40% every month just to cover the membership fee\*\*, before making any actual profit.    
Even at a very strong 10% monthly return, you would need around USD $2,000 invested merely to break even. At a 5% return, you would need USD $4,000, and at 2%, USD $10,000—while still carrying the risk of losses and drawdowns.

Members are also told that the system should be tested for at least six to twelve months. That means paying USD $1,200–$2,400 in fees while also committing enough trading capital to make the returns meaningful. That is a substantial amount of money to trial a system that, in my opinion, does not yet have solid, independently verified long-term results.

To be fair, the membership also includes courses and access to a community, which may have value for people wanting education and active involvement. However, if you are mainly joining because you want a reliable, passive AI trading system, my experience was that it was not truly passive, predictable or consistent.

There is also a recruitment incentive. Members could avoid paying their membership fee by recruiting four paying members. In my opinion, this creates an MLM-style incentive and means some recommendations may come from people who financially benefit from recruiting     
others.

My personal experience with the upline was also concerning. Once it became clear that I was not interested in recruiting more people, I was largely ignored and unsupported. This made me question whether the emphasis was genuinely on teaching members and helping them achieve good outcomes, or primarily on expanding the recruitment structure and generating more membership revenue.

They present the community as caring and supportive, but I did not feel cared for when I raised genuine concerns and was no longer useful as a potential recruiter. From my perspective, the strongest attention appeared to go toward recruitment and promotion rather than accountability, consistent education or helping members understand why their results differed so significantly.

The system may eventually become profitable, and these concerns might be easier to accept if the membership fee were much lower. However, at USD $200 per month, the capital and returns required simply to break even are significant.

I’m posting this because I want others to understand the financial commitment before risking their capital as I did. Calculate the return needed after fees, ask for independently verified live results and understand that your results may vary significantly from those being promoted.
